text:
emma: Heads-up — enterprise customer reported intermittent 401s on signed callback endpoint after their IdP rotated keys last night. They see about 1 in 20 requests fail, then succeed on retry. Customer name: AcmeCorp.

morgan: Can you paste the failure log lines and the exact error? 401 from our API or 401 returned from their callback receiver?

emma: 401 from our Verify layer. Logs show two patterns: "kid not found in JWKS" and "signature verification failed". Sometimes a subsequent retry within a few seconds succeeds.

samir: That smells like a propagation/caching window. Our JWKS cache TTL is 5m with stale-while-revalidate enabled. If their IdP rotated and returned 200 without cache-control, our edge may keep old keys until revalidate.

kevin: Also worth checking node clock skew. If a node's clock is behind, Verify can reject tokens due to nbf/exp checks. Last time we saw this the skew was ~90s on an autoscaled instance.

morgan: Agreed. Requesting: (1) original raw JWT header (base64), (2) X-Request-ID from failing attempts, (3) the JWKS URL they use and any cache headers from a curl to that URL.

emma: Sending samples now — attached in support case. Example curl they used to repro:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 9f3b-..." \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/callback
```

morgan: From the sample JWKS response they gave, the HTTP response lacked Cache-Control and ETag headers. Our cache did a 200 earlier and then didn't refresh until TTL expired. If the IdP returned the new key but some of our nodes still had the old cached object, kid lookups will fail.

samir: I pulled node logs for the X-Request-ID — one failing request hit node-a which had a cached jwks.json last-fetched at 1718323900, node-b that later succeeded fetched at 1718324700 (after background refresh). Node-a's system time was fine. That suggests our cache invalidation on key-miss isn't aggressive enough.

kevin: Short mitigation: increase leeway in JWT verification to 60s and implement immediate on-miss JWKS fetch (sync) when kid not found, but with a rate limit to avoid hammering IdP. We should also special-case key-miss to trigger background refresh across the pool.

morgan: I can push a small change: on KeyNotFound -> synchronous fetch from JWKS and then retry verification once. Falling back to background async if fetch fails. Also add a counter metric for KeyNotFound->refetch. Will create PR and request quick canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for eng-runtime key-miss-refetch (canary to 10%).

emma: Customer asked for repro steps they can run to validate if our fix helps. Suggested: fire a single request with an old cached token and then rotate keys on their IdP, then call new token and old token within 30s — they saw intermittent failures.

morgan: For support doc, I'm drafting quick repro steps and a checklist: 1) confirm JWKS URL cache headers; 2) capture JWT header and kid; 3) look for 401 patterns and node ids; 4) if KeyNotFound, force refetch and check whether new key is present.

kevin: After canary, we should watch metric: runtime.jwks.key_miss_refetch{env=prod} and token_verification.errors with label reason=kid_not_found. Alert if spike > 5/min.

samir: Ops note: also check our CDN in front of IdP (if they use one) — some customers have intermediate caches that return stale jwks even when origin rotated.

emma: I'll update the support ticket with the mitigation and ETA for the canary. Customer is okay to wait for a patch, but wants monitoring and a postmortem if it recurs.

morgan: PR opened -> https://git.internal/repo/eng-runtime/pulls/432. Can we get a quick review from infra? @samir @kevin

samir: Reviewing now. If all good we'll promote from canary to 50% in 30m.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary 10% healthy.

kevin: I'll add a temporary leeway config flag in runtime config to allow support to increase for this customer if needed. Not permanent.

emma: Thanks team. I'll follow up after canary and attach customer logs. :thumbsup: :eyes:
